section1.heading: 1. General Provisions
section1.paragraph1: This Privacy Policy explains how OÜ Küberloome processes personal data when you use the Sotsiaal.pro web platform. It covers account creation, sign-in, subscriptions, chats, rooms, help requests and offers, documents, deep research, file uploads, logs, and other platform workflows. It also explains what data is stored, for how long, how feature limits and storage quotas can affect retention, and which automated systems are used to generate responses, drafts, classifications, or search results.
section1.paragraph2: Sotsiaal.pro processes personal data in accordance with the Estonian Personal Data Protection Act and the EU General Data Protection Regulation. If you have questions about data processing, contact us before continuing to use the service.

section2.heading: 2. Data We Collect
section2.paragraph1: 2.1 Account and authentication data. We process your email address, user role, password/PIN hash, email verification state, temporary sign-in tokens, one-time code records, trusted-device data, and any profile data you choose to add or update.
section2.paragraph2:
2.2 Service usage data. We process conversations and conversation messages, room messages and membership data, help requests, help offers, help matches, research requests and job metadata, document uploads, temporary chat files, agent drafts and final outputs, invites, subscription and sponsored-access status, payment metadata, audit records, and storage- or quota-related metadata needed to run those workflows.

When professional work tools are used, we also process their content and metadata: covision discussions and summaries; supervision process meetings, agreements, and outputs; mentoring relationship agreements and meetings; field work visit data and notes; the specialist’s private reflection entries; well-being records and checkpoints; Journey summaries; and records of sharing meeting summaries to a room and of approval rounds. For a voice call in a room we process call metadata and participants’ consents; the call itself is not recorded. Files of a data copy requested by the user are time-limited.
section2.paragraph3: 2.3 Technical and local data. We process IP address, browser and device information, usage, rate-limit, and error logs, security events, and technical events related to AI, search, and speech features. The platform also uses essential cookies and browser storage to keep language, accessibility settings, active conversation state, PIN keypad preferences, and other usability settings.

section3.heading: 3. Purposes and Legal Bases
section3.items:
• Account creation, sign-in, role handling, subscription management, and core platform features are processed for the performance of a contract (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)).
  • Payments, fraud prevention, security checks, logging, and service reliability are processed for the performance of a contract and for legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(b),(f)).
  • Compliance with legal obligations, accounting, and claim defense are processed on the basis of legal obligation and legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(c),(f)).
  • Microphone access, browser speech, and device-local storage are used only when the user triggers or allows the relevant feature.
  • Help listings, rooms, and invite flows are processed to operate the service and to mediate communication initiated by the user.

section4.heading: 4. How Platform Content Is Used
section4.body:
4.1 Chats and rooms. Chat and room messages are used to generate responses, show history, and enable collaboration. A conversation can also contain workflow state, such as whether it is locked into document drafting, a help request, a help offer flow, or a deep research task.

4.2 Help requests, help offers, and matching. When you save a help request or help offer, it becomes visible to other users in the relevant listing views according to the platform workflow. When you connect a request and an offer, the platform creates or reopens a room and shares the necessary details with the involved parties.

4.3 Documents and agent outputs. Files uploaded to Documents and the drafts or final outputs created from them are stored in the user's workspace until deleted by the user, removed with the account, or cleaned up under retention or storage-quota rules. They are not made public to other users unless the user explicitly shares them through platform actions.

4.4 Temporary chat files. Files added in the chat document workflow or analysis flow are meant only for that specific conversation or session. They are not automatically added to the persistent Documents library unless the user separately uses the document-library workflow.

4.5 Voice features. Dictation audio is processed only to create text. Read-aloud uses chat text to produce audio playback. These features are not used for marketing or user profiling.

4.6 Automated processing. Some workflows use automated systems to route conversations, classify requests, retrieve documents, rank results, and generate responses or drafts. These systems support the service but do not replace the user's own judgment or create solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

4.8 Privacy pre-checks. In sensitive workflows, the platform may use local or server-side pre-checks that detect simple signals of personal data, contact details, personal identification numbers, addresses, child-safety concerns, or crisis risk. This helps warn the user and minimise data, but it is not full anonymisation or a legal compliance certification.

4.9 Role-based access. More sensitive capabilities are made available based on role, organisation, professional-use confirmation, and technical permissions. An administrator or organisation role does not by default grant access to a user's private conversations, documents, or files.

section5.heading: 5. Processors
section5.body:
Sotsiaal.pro uses processors where needed to provide the service, for example payment processing, email delivery, AI and speech services, hosting, and logging infrastructure. Processors handle data only under Sotsiaal.pro's instructions and subject to contractual and technical safeguards.

Read-aloud. When a user presses the listen button on an answer, the text to be read is sent to a speech synthesis service. For Estonian read-aloud this is the University of Tartu service (TartuNLP), located in Estonia. Only the text being read is sent — no account, email address or other identifier is sent with it. Read-aloud never starts on its own. English and Russian read-aloud uses the user's own browser speech synthesis, and the platform does not send that text to any service provider.

section6.heading: 6. Data Disclosure and Sharing
section6.body:
Sotsiaal.pro does not sell personal data. Data is shared only to the extent needed to run the service: with processors, with the payment provider, with users you invite or are matched with in rooms and help-mediation workflows, and with competent authorities where required by law.

A user's personal conversations and documents are linked to that user's account. Room and group conversation content is visible to room members, and only to the extent needed for the relevant workflow. An organisation or employer administrator is not automatically given general access to an employee's personal conversations, documents, or files.

Platform administrator access to content is exceptional technical administration access used only where justified, for example to provide support, investigate an error or security incident, maintain service reliability, prevent abuse, or comply with a legal claim or obligation.

If you create an invite, save a visible help listing, or connect parties through a room, the relevant information is shared inside the platform only with the users for whom that workflow is intended.

If a user or organisation representative accepts a professional-use or data-processing framework, evidence records related to that acceptance may be retained and, where necessary, shared with the relevant organisation or user to prove the existence, version, and time of acceptance.

section7.heading: 7. Retention
section7.body:
7.1 Account and profile data. Account and profile data is generally retained until the account is deleted, except where the law requires longer retention.

7.2 Temporary authentication data. An email verification link is generally retained for up to 24 hours, a PIN reset token for up to 60 minutes, a one-time sign-in code for up to 15 minutes, a temporary sign-in token for up to 15 minutes, and a trusted-device record for up to 30 days. Expired authentication records are removed regularly.

7.3 Conversations and current work data. Conversations, chat messages, current conversation state records, and general usage logs are generally retained for up to 90 days from the last activity or from the relevant record's creation or update time.

7.4 Rooms and help data. Inactive rooms and related messages are generally retained for up to 90 days after the last substantive activity. Closed, cancelled, or archived help requests and help offers, and completed or rejected matches, are generally retained for up to 90 days after the last update.

7.5 Documents and agent outputs. Files uploaded to the document library, templates, document drafting workspace drafts, and confirmed agent outputs are generally retained for up to 90 days from the last modification. If an older document is technically linked to a newer output, it may be retained briefly until the newer link ends.

7.6 Deletion and deletion-job tracking. When a user deletes a document, it is removed from active document management and deletion of the related file and RAG or search-index reference is triggered where such a reference exists. If deletion from an external index does not succeed immediately, a technical deletion-job record may remain so that a failed or pending deletion is visible and can be followed up.

7.7 Account deletion. When an account is deleted, the user account and related active user data are removed according to the application's deletion logic. Technical audit records and deletion-job records may remain as limited metadata to prove the deletion action, handle pending deletion jobs, maintain security, or comply with legal obligations. A delivered pre-inquiry leaves the recipient an anonymised fact record and their own work notes; the author's content is deleted.

7.8 Backups and operational logs. If content is deleted by the user, the account is deleted, or a record is removed because of quota or cleanup rules, it may briefly remain in backups, system or proxy logs, or service-provider technical logs for recovery, security, troubleshooting, or legal-compliance purposes, and is then removed or anonymised according to the relevant operations or provider configuration.

7.9 Audits, acceptances, and payments. General document audit records, technical processing logs, and evidence records related to professional-use or data-processing frameworks are generally retained for up to 90 days, unless a longer period is reasonably needed to prove a specific acceptance, contractual relationship, or legal obligation. A detailed raw response or payload received from the payment provider is generally truncated or removed after 90 days. The minimal payment and accounting record is retained for up to 7 years or longer if required by applicable law.

7.10 Content of professional work tools. The content of covision, supervision, mentoring, reflections, well-being records, and the Journey is kept while the service is used or until the user deletes it, and is deleted together with the account upon account deletion. Field work visit data is subject to the general 90-day retention period. Data copy files are deleted automatically after they expire. CaseWorkAssist is the worker’s private work tool: an archived case and all its content are deleted 12 calendar months after archiving, and the worker is warned 30 days before deletion. The content of a transferred draft is deleted no later than 12 calendar months after transfer; the content-free draft row, transfer fact and list of fields remain only until the case or account is deleted. An organisation may agree only to a shorter period.

section7Support.body: 7.11 Wellbeing support sharing. Unopened shared content is retained for up to 30 days. Opened or corrected content remains until closure and for up to 90 further days, but never beyond 12 months from first sending; recall deletes content immediately. Deleting the recipient membership or organisation ends access and deletes content. Account deletion recalls an unopened message; an already opened copy may remain with the recipient until the same short deadline. After content deletion, a restricted contentless sharing receipt remains for three years. Only material necessary for a concrete dispute may be placed under a separate legal hold.

section7Supervision.body: 7.12 Shared supervision evidence. As an exception to the general rule in section 7.10, closing an account deletes the user's private supervision preparation area and personal persistent output. The shared supervision process, contract versions and acceptance facts, approved summaries, closure record, and content-free audit trail remain as evidence shared by the other participants without the deleted user's identity. Until a specific retention period is approved, these records remain in AWAITING_POLICY status and are not purged automatically.

section8.items:
• Right to access your personal data and obtain a copy.
  • Right to correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
  • Right to request erasure where there is a legal basis for it.
  • Right to restrict processing or object to processing based on legitimate interest.
  • Right to data portability, where the GDPR conditions for portability are met.

section9.heading: 9. Cookies and Browser Storage
section9.body: Sotsiaal.pro uses essential cookies and browser storage for sign-in, session handling, language, accessibility, trusted-device state, active conversation state, and other usability preferences. We do not use advertising cookies or third-party marketing trackers. The public product UI also does not currently use advertising trackers.

section10.heading: 10. Security
section10.body:
We apply risk-based technical and organisational safeguards, including encrypted connections, protection for PINs and one-time codes, role-based access, permission checks, logical separation of documents and workflows, security and audit logs, and expiry and deletion flows. Access to data is limited by work task and system need.

We minimise personal data in technical logs and audit records: the aim is to store mainly technical metadata, such as event type, user or resource technical identifier, status, time, file type, or size. Application logs are not intended to store document content, conversation content, voice-data buffers, request body previews, raw payment-provider payloads, or authentication or invite token values.

No web service is entirely risk-free. Server backups, systemd/journald logs, proxy logs, and external service-provider technical logs depend on separate operations and provider configurations. For that reason, we recommend entering only the data needed for the workflow at hand.

section11.heading: 11. Changes
section11.body: This Privacy Policy may be updated if platform features, data flows, or legal requirements change. Significant changes will be communicated in the product or by email.

privacy_filter.heading: 4.10 Privacy pre-check and Privacy Filter
privacy_filter.body:
In sensitive workflows, the platform may use a privacy pre-check to detect and mask possible personal data before AI processing, RAG indexing, document drafting, logging, or saving a public help listing. The check may rely on Sotsiaal.pro's local pattern-based filter and, where deployed, the locally running OpenAI Privacy Filter model.

If possible personal data is detected in the user input, the system may offer choices: the user can edit the text, the system can send a masked version, or in a private professional workflow the original text can be sent after the user's explicit choice. Public help requests and help offers use stricter data minimisation, and continuing with the original sensitive text may be restricted.

The privacy pre-check does not guarantee that every personal-data item or sensitive detail will always be detected. It is an additional safeguard that helps reduce accidental excessive processing; the user and, where relevant, the organisation must still assess the legal basis, necessity of the data, and appropriate workflow.

section1.heading: 1. General Provisions
section1.body:
These Terms of Use govern the use of the Sotsiaal.pro platform operated by OÜ Küberloome. By using the platform, you confirm that you have read and accepted these Terms.

To keep the service stable, secure, and reasonably usable, the platform may apply technical limits and usage rules. section2.heading: 2. Service Description
section2.body:
Sotsiaal.pro is a role-based web platform where a user can ask questions in chat, continue in guidance mode, describe help requests and help offers, use document workflows, manage documents, open rooms, send invites, and use profile, subscription, and accessibility settings.

The platform combines AI, retrieval-based knowledge access, and user-selected workflows to support both social work professionals and people seeking help. It is not an emergency channel and does not replace binding official decisions, professional advice, or urgent assistance.

For professional roles, additional work tools are available, such as covision, supervision, mentoring, field work, reflections, well-being views, and personal search. Voice calls can be held in rooms with the parties’ consent; calls are not recorded.

section3.heading: 3. Account and Access
section3.items:
• You must create an account and choose an appropriate role to use the core platform features.
  • You must keep your email, PIN, and other sign-in information confidential and are responsible for actions taken through your account.
  • Sign-in may require an extra confirmation sent by email, and you may choose to trust a device for future sign-ins.
  • Many workflows require an active subscription or valid sponsored access.
  • Administrator preview mode or other administrative rights do not grant the right to impersonate another user, view that user's personal conversations or documents, or modify that user's data without a clear legal or technical justification.

section6.body:

At present, the service applies the following technical limits: up to 50 user turns in one chat; deep research limited to one active job per user and a plan-based monthly usage allowance; the same document may be refined or corrected up to 3 times in a row; and materials may be uploaded up to 10 files at a time and up to 100 MB per day.

Sotsiaal.pro may apply technical limits, reasonable-use controls, and abuse-prevention measures to protect service operation, security, and fair access. If usage is unusually heavy, repetitive, or appears to bypass limits, Sotsiaal.pro may temporarily slow, restrict, pause, or reconfigure affected features even if the account itself remains active.

section7.heading: 7. Platform Workflows and Results
section7.body:
Sotsiaal.pro supports users through the platform's chat, document, help, and room workflows as described on the platform.

In situations involving crisis, violence, child safety, or self-harm risk, the platform may display urgent-help guidance and route the user toward an Estonian support channel or a competent person. This routing does not replace emergency services, child protection, victim support, or professional help.

section8.heading: 8. Professional Use and Processing Framework
section8.body:
Sotsiaal.pro may be used as a private individual and also as a work tool in workflows where no identifiable personal data of a client or other data subject is entered.

If a user wishes to use Sotsiaal.pro on behalf of an employer or organisation with identifiable personal data of a client or other data subject, the user must have clear permission from the employer or organisation and, where necessary, a separate contractual data processing framework.

An organisation or employer administrator role does not by itself provide general access to an employee's personal conversations, documents, or files. Room and group conversation content is visible to room members, and data shared by a user is handled according to the visibility rules of the relevant workflow.

Internal confirmations, instructions, or usage permissions between employer and employee do not by themselves create a processor relationship between Sotsiaal.pro and the organisation. If Sotsiaal.pro processes personal data on behalf of an organisation, there must also be a written or electronic contractual framework bindingly accepted by Sotsiaal.pro.

Sotsiaal.pro may make available on the platform a standard framework document for professional use and data processing or similar terms. Reading such a document, downloading it, or confirming it at employee level does not automatically make it binding on the organisation. If the document is intended to serve as a framework for processing data on behalf of an organisation, it becomes binding on the organisation only after proper signing or other provable electronic acceptance.

For professional use, the organisation should define roles, permissions, allowed data categories, data minimisation rules, review and confirmation procedures, and audit-trail needs before sensitive workflows are used. More sensitive capabilities may be limited to specialists, service providers, municipalities, or organisation-linked users.

section9.heading: 9. Use of AI
section9.paragraph1:
Sotsiaal.pro uses AI, retrieval-backed knowledge access, and other technical services to answer questions, provide guidance, help draft documents, and support help-request and help-offer workflows. The platform may ask the user to confirm in chat which work mode the current conversation should continue in.

The AI may propose the most likely work mode, answer, classification, match, or draft, but the final decision to continue the workflow and use the output remains with the user. The user understands that AI output may be inaccurate, incomplete, or require correction.
section9.paragraph2:
AI output must not be treated as automatically binding truth, an official position, a professional decision, or the sole basis for a decision.

The platform informs the user that they are interacting with AI functions unless this is already clear from the nature of the workflow or the user interface.

section10.heading: 10. Data Processing in Chats and Uploaded Materials
section10.paragraph1: When using the platform, a user may enter text, send room messages, save help data, invite other people, upload documents, or use voice features. That data is processed to operate the service in accordance with the Privacy Policy.
section10.paragraph2: More detailed rules on data processing, retention periods, deletion-job tracking, logging minimisation, and user rights are described in the Privacy Policy.
section10.items:
• Chat and room content. Conversations, rooms, and their related workflow state are stored to operate the platform, show history, and continue the features chosen by the user. A user's personal conversations are linked to that user's account, and room content is visible to room members.
  • Help listings and invites. The user is responsible for sharing only the data needed to connect with another person or mediate help.
  • Temporary chat files. Files added in the chat document workflow or analysis flow are intended for that session or workflow and are not automatically added to the persistent Documents library.
  • Documents library and agent outputs. If the user uploads a file into the persistent Documents library or approves an agent result, it is generally stored for up to 90 days from the last change, unless the law or a technical link requires a different retention period for a short time. When a document is deleted, it is removed from active document management and deletion of the related file and RAG or search-index reference is triggered where such a reference exists.
  • Account deletion and technical records. When an account is deleted, the user loses access to related active data and the account is removed according to the application's deletion logic. Limited technical audit records and deletion-job records may remain for security, proof of deletion, handling pending deletion jobs, or legal obligations.
  • Dictation and read-aloud. Voice features are used only to provide that feature. The user must ensure they have the right to transmit another person's data through a microphone or file.
  • Sensitive data. If the user enters sensitive information or data about third parties, the user is responsible for having a lawful basis and for sharing only the minimum necessary information.
  • Logging and audit. The platform may store technical logs, audit records, and deletion-job records for service security, reliability, and legal obligations. Application logs are not intended to store document content, conversation content, voice-data buffers, request body previews, raw payment-provider payloads, or authentication or invite token values.
  • Professional-use confirmations. If the user or an organisation representative accepts a professional-use or data processing framework, the platform may store proof records related to that confirmation, including the time, version, role, and other technical details needed for evidence.

privacy_filter.heading: 10.1 Privacy pre-check and masking
privacy_filter.body:
Before AI processing, RAG search, document drafting, logging, or saving a public help listing, Sotsiaal.pro may check whether the input contains personal data or other sensitive information. The check may use the platform's own local rules and, where deployed on the server, the locally running OpenAI Privacy Filter model.

If the check finds a name, personal identification code, address, phone number, email address, or another identifiable detail, the platform may show a warning and offer choices: edit the text, send a masked version, or continue with the original text in an allowed private workflow. Continuing with the original sensitive text may not be available for public help requests or help offers.

Masking is a data-minimisation aid, not full anonymisation or a legal guarantee. The user remains responsible for ensuring that the information entered is necessary for the workflow and that there is an appropriate basis for processing it.

intro.paragraph1: Sotsiaal.pro is a next-generation support platform for the social sector that provides trustworthy information, AI support, practical tools, and communication options in one digital environment. The platform is intended for people seeking clarity in life-related questions, social-sector professionals, and service providers.
intro.paragraph2: The social sector is characterised by heavy workloads, fragmented information, and difficult navigation across the system of services, benefits, and contacts - as also noted by the OSKA report (2025). Sotsiaal.pro aims to make social-sector knowledge more accessible and understandable, simplify workflows, and help people gain a clearer understanding of their situation. To do this, the platform brings together social-sector sources, guidance, legal frameworks, methodologies, and practical materials.
intro.paragraph3: The central place to use the platform is the chat window, where users can describe a situation, ask about services, benefits, rights, and professional practice, and clarify possible next steps. AI helps surface relevant options, explain connections, and prepare useful texts and next steps. Sources are shown with answers so the information can be checked. From the same page, users can also start separate workflows, such as help requests, help offers, deep research, pre-inquiries, and document analysis.
intro.paragraph4: Sotsiaal.pro is built on the principle that AI does not replace a specialist or make the final decision for a person. AI helps people reach knowledge, rights, services, and work tools faster, but sensitive data, crisis situations, child and youth safety, and professional decisions require human review, clear role boundaries, and, when needed, routing to real support channels.
intro.paragraph5: Chat rooms are separate communication spaces where a person seeking help, a social work professional, a service provider, or a colleague can be invited. A room may be created, for example, after matching a request for help with an offer of help or after sharing a request, so that the parties can continue communication and clarify next steps.
intro.paragraph6: The service map is Sotsiaal.pro's map-based application that helps users find social-sector points of contact and contact details. At first, the service map focuses on local-government social welfare contacts and service providers so that the necessary information and situation-related options are more visible to the user.
intro.paragraph7: Our vision is to become a digital environment for the social sector that connects trustworthy information, practical tools, service providers, and communication. Sotsiaal.pro supports people in different life and work situations - whether the question is related to finding a service, benefit, document, request for help or offer of help, career counselling, job opportunity, or assistive aid.
intro.paragraph8: Sotsiaal.pro is being developed as a social enterprise and a social innovation initiative. We combine technology and social-sector practice to reduce information barriers and make workflows, collaboration, and finding help clearer, faster, and more accessible. author.title: From one idea to a real platform
author.byline: Laur Raudsoo, owner and management board member
paragraphs: The story of Sotsiaal.pro began in 2017 with the wish to create the sotsiaalinfo.ee portal. At the time I did not yet have a long employment history in the social field, but a practical connection with it had already taken shape through studies, work, internships and professional volunteering. I had just completed a bachelor's degree in social work at Tallinn University, been active in the Estonian Association of Social Workers, worked as a personal assistant, been involved in the platform development and international cooperation of the NGO Helpific, and completed an internship at the Ministry of Social Affairs focused on analysing benefits and allowances for people with disabilities. That same year I began working as the managing editor of the journal Sotsiaaltöö.

The idea grew out of my contact with the social field, accessibility, digital solutions and social entrepreneurship. Even then the starting point was clear: the same environment cannot speak to everyone in the same way. A social-field specialist needs a deeper knowledge space and professional tools, while a person turning to it with a life question needs clear, understandable and accessible support.

This led early on to the idea of a solution that unites both sides while taking the needs of each into account. One side was to gather the professional content a specialist needs — practices, the journal Sotsiaaltöö, research, guidance materials, legislation, court decisions, events and cooperation partners. The other side took shape as an environment centred on help that is understandable and practical for the person.

The next significant step came in 2020, when the idea moved towards a social-assistance mobile application. The central question became how a person can reach services, benefits and applying for help in a simpler, clearer and more practical way. It was at this stage that the idea of applying artificial intelligence on the platform emerged — roughly two years before ChatGPT reached the public.

A few years later, by 2022, the vision had become considerably clearer and more complete. On the one hand, the idea of a platform for social workers took shape, supporting covision, the discussion of anonymised cases and professional cooperation. On the other hand, the direction where a person with a life question could more easily reach the necessary information, services and next steps remained just as important.

At the same time, the role of artificial intelligence became more concrete: AI was seen as an assistant that could reduce workload, analyse data, support prevention, help resolve cases and offer clearer support to a person with a life question. A more complete vision of a digital solution began to form, in which the specialist's workflows, the user journey of a person with a life question, data and the possibilities of artificial intelligence make up an interconnected whole.

Actual development work began in May 2025. By then, the earlier portal and mobile-app ideas had evolved into a single solution that can be used on both computers and mobile devices and also installed as an app. The aim of the development was to turn the vision shaped over the years into a solution where both the specialist and the person with a life question have their own logic, materials and workflows. Alongside this, the gathering of the platform's knowledge and materials began, on which the artificial-intelligence assistants can rely when answering.

Almost a year later, by April 2026, the original idea had grown into a broad support and work platform for the social sector: Sotsiaal.pro. The platform includes two AI assistants: one for social-sector specialists and one for people seeking help with life questions. They help users find information, get guidance and move on to next steps. Alongside the assistants, users can work across different modes, agents and workflows—for example, drafting documents and texts, managing files, analysing materials and conducting in-depth research. Specialists can also use shared rooms for collaboration, covision and, when appropriate, communication with clients.
The platform also lets you describe both voluntary and paid help requests and help offers and turn them into listings with the help of AI. This feature is free for all platform users.

To support accessibility, the user can adjust the platform's language, contrast, text size, theme, screen profile, and motion and performance settings. In conversations, dictation and read-aloud are also available, making the platform more flexible to use across different needs, devices and situations.

Sotsiaal.pro aims to help people find support and social-sector professionals do their work. The platform brings together knowledge from the field, practical tools, and opportunities to connect people who need help with those who offer it. We are developing it into a comprehensive environment where people can also find support with finances, work, housing, and assistive aids.

The story of Sotsiaal.pro is a journey of nearly ten years from the first idea to a working solution. It reflects both social entrepreneurship and innovation: the platform is being developed deliberately and carefully so that Sotsiaal.pro grows into a genuinely valuable, well-functioning and secure platform that could reach the pocket of every Estonian.

features_page.title: Sotsiaal.pro features
features_page.intro: This page summarises Sotsiaal.pro's core functions: what each feature does, who it is for, and which privacy, safety, and human-review principles apply in the workflows.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.body: The workspace is a role-based overview and work area that shows the tools suited to the user's role. The help-seeker view focuses on help requests and offers, pre-inquiries, document drafting, invites, and the service map. The social work professional view adds documents, inquiry intake, co-vision, and materials. The service provider view adds the service profile, pre-inquiry intake, and visibility related to the service map. Some tools may require active access or a subscription.

help.title: Help requests and help offers
help.body: The user describes a help request or help offer in their own words. Sotsiaal.pro helps make the description clearer, asks follow-up questions when needed, and prepares the listing for publication. After the listing is confirmed, the platform shows suitable help requests or help offers based on category, region, form of help, and other signals. When the user connects two suitable listings, a shared chat room is created for the parties to continue communication.

service_card.title: Service card
service_card.body: The service card is Sotsiaal.pro's map view for finding published local-government social-welfare contacts and service providers. Users can search by name, description, address, service, category, target group, or area. Search also uses the services, service locations, descriptions, and price information listed under a service provider profile. Markers are created by location: one service location can show several services, and the same service can be linked to several locations.

journey.title: Journey
journey.body: Journey keeps a situation summary, related topics, missing information, careful notes, and suggested next steps together. The journey is private at first and is not shared with a specialist, service provider, or another party before the user knowingly confirms sharing.

knowledge_base.title: Sotsiaal.pro knowledge base
knowledge_base.body: The Sotsiaal.pro knowledge base is a background layer that supports assistant answers with domain information. It includes municipal service and contact information, application forms, legal acts, guidance, methodology materials, organisation and service-provider information, practical materials, and field articles or studies. Automated checks and update workflows help detect changes in municipal, Riigi Teataja, and contact-information sources and refresh content in a controlled way. This helps keep answers in a social-sector context and reduces the need to search for the same information manually across separate places.

assistants_agents.title: Sotsiaal.pro assistants and agents
assistants_agents.body: Sotsiaal.pro assistants and agents support users as they work with a question, document, or situation description. The conversation supports asking for information, making sense of a situation, and user-selected workflows such as document drafting, document analysis, deep research, a pre-inquiry, a help request, or a help offer. The user decides which tool to use. The assistant can help organize information, clarify questions, and prepare content when needed.

sources.title: Source display
sources.body: When sources are available for an answer, the sources button opens an overview of the materials the answer relies on. This helps check whether the information comes from legislation, guidance, a local-government website, service information, or another material used. In social-sector questions, visible sources help assess whether the answer is sufficiently checkable and up to date.

drafting.title: Document drafting
drafting.body: Document drafting is a workspace for creating letters, applications, reports, summaries, and completed form outputs. The user can create a draft from source documents, a template, and instructions, or use an audio-file workflow: select a call recording or upload an audio file, create a separate transcript, review the transcript, and only then create an accurate summary. Speech or audio-file content is not added to the draft automatically. The draft stays in the workspace for review, refinement, saving, and approval. An approved result can be downloaded as a DOCX or PDF file.

analysis.title: Document analysis
analysis.body: Document analysis starts from the file uploaded by the user. Sotsiaal.pro extracts text from the file, splits it into parts suitable for analysis, and answers the user’s questions based on the document content. It is useful for understanding, summarising, and finding important points in an official response, guide, contract, report, decision, or another document. By default, the analysis focuses on the uploaded document. In extended analysis, the user may add domain context from the Sotsiaal.pro knowledge base. A file added in chat is temporary and is not automatically moved to the Documents library.

research.title: Deep research
research.body: Deep research helps prepare a more thorough overview of a social-sector topic, service, law, guide, or practical question. Sotsiaal.pro searches related sources, gathers the information into a structured answer or working report draft, and highlights the main observations, connections, gaps, and possible next steps.

rooms.title: Chat rooms
rooms.body: Chat rooms are shared communication spaces where the user may invite a person seeking help, a social work professional, a service provider, or a colleague. A room may be created when a help request and help offer are connected, or after a pre-inquiry when the parties need clarification and further communication. In a room, members can continue the text conversation and, when needed, start an audio-only call between the same room members. Calls are not recorded by default; recording is a separate consent-based workflow, and transcription is started later only as a separate user action. A regular invite adds the person to the room. If needed, the inviter may pay for one month of role-based platform access for the invited person.

documents.title: Documents: storage and management
documents.body: The documents view brings together the user’s working files, background materials, templates, and document-agent drafts and approved results. Each file can be assigned a role, such as background material or template, and allowed for use in document drafting. Created results can be opened, copied, deleted, and downloaded after approval.

pre_inquiry.title: Pre-inquiry
pre_inquiry.body: A pre-inquiry can start in three ways: describing the situation in the user's own words, answering a shorter problem-focused pre-assessment, or completing a more detailed pre-assessment. When starting with questions, the workflow gathers information by life domain about daily functioning, health, living environment, support network, previous help, the person's own wishes, and main needs. The workflow helps notice possible risks and excessive personal data, then creates a reviewable summary and inquiry draft. When there is enough information, Sotsiaal.pro looks through service-map data for possible municipal social-sector contacts or service providers based on the description and area. The user can edit, save, copy, download, or open the draft as an email. When internal Sotsiaal.pro intake is available, the recipient can open the inquiry in the platform, download the pre-assessment details, and continue in a chat room if needed.

intake.title: Inquiry intake
intake.body: Inquiry intake is a workspace for a social work professional or service provider who allows pre-inquiries to be received in the platform. It receives pre-inquiries confirmed by the user and addressed to a specific account or service profile. The recipient can see the situation description, addressee, and inquiry draft, mark the inquiry as accepted, and open a chat room with the parties when needed.

kovisioon.title: Co-vision and practice examples
kovisioon.body: The co-vision view is workflow-based: the home view separates starting a new co-vision, my co-visions, and practice examples. When creating a new co-vision, the case owner moves step by step through basic information, the anonymous situation description, the situation flow, the network, risks, protective factors, and the central question and expectation. After saving, the co-vision room opens with the case canvas at the centre, rather than a long form or a regular chat. In the room, the canvas brings together the central question, situation description, situation flow, network, risks, protective factors, questions, reflections, suggestions, next steps, and summary. Participants can add written questions, reflections, suggestions, and next-step proposals, invite participants, use the request-to-speak queue, and hold an audio conversation without recording. Co-vision audio is not recorded, not transcribed, and not used for the summary; the summary is based on the case canvas and written discussion. Practice examples remain a separate area where users can add generalised effective-practice entries or create one from a co-vision, and a published practice example remains subject to anonymity checks and review before use.

wellbeing.title: Work wellbeing
wellbeing.body: Work wellbeing tools help a social-sector specialist notice workload, emotional load, recovery needs, recurring interruptions, and the effect of difficult cases. The workspace can later support quick checks, weekly or monthly overviews, difficult-case notes, workplace-violence situations, recovery, work boundaries, interruptions, work processes, role boundaries, and starter support.

wellbeing_quick_check.title: Quick check
wellbeing_quick_check.body: The quick check helps you notice workload, recovery, and emotional strain, then choose one small next step.

materials_adding.title: Adding materials
materials_adding.body: Adding materials lets a professional or service provider send files to supplement the Sotsiaal.pro knowledge base, for example guides, service descriptions, forms, or other sources. A comment can be added to help explain the material's context. Submitted material goes into review and is not added to the knowledge base automatically. After review, it is decided whether the material is suitable for adding to the knowledge base.

service_card_listing.title: Service provider card profile
service_card_listing.body: The service provider card profile makes the service provider visible on the service card. The card can show the provider's location or service area, main services, target groups, and contact details, so the user can find the right place to turn to faster.

service_profile.title: Service profile and management
service_profile.body: The service profile is the service provider's workspace for managing public information and inquiries. The profile can describe the organisation's general information, contacts, service area, accessibility, service locations, and separate service records. Each service can have its own description, target group, area, price, contact, and pre-inquiry settings, and it can be linked to one or more service locations. Published profile, service, and location information can be used on the service map and in the knowledge base.

privacy_safety.title: Privacy pre-check
privacy_safety.body: The privacy pre-layer helps notice excessive personal data in sensitive workflows before text is sent, processed by AI, saved, or shared. The check looks for simple signals such as an email address, phone number, personal identification code, or address, and shows a warning with a masked version when needed. The aim is to keep only the information the selected workflow needs in the input. It is a support layer and does not replace the user’s or organisation’s data-protection decision.

crisis_routing.title: Crisis and risk routing
crisis_routing.body: When a user describes immediate danger, self-harm or suicide risk, violence, or another serious crisis, Sotsiaal.pro shows urgent-help guidance and Estonian support channels. These include 112, Child Helpline 116 111, and Victim Support 116 006. AI does not replace emergency services, child protection, victim support, or professional crisis help.

youth_child_safety.title: Youth and child safety
youth_child_safety.body: Signals related to minors, child protection, school bullying, domestic violence, abuse, or neglect are treated as a higher-risk workflow. AI may help structure the situation, but it does not make the final risk assessment or replace child protection, emergency services, or a specialist decision.

trusted_access_security.title: Role-based access and account security
trusted_access_security.body: More sensitive workflows are not the same for everyone. Help seekers, specialists, service providers, municipalities, and administrators have different visibility and permissions; professional use requires clearer roles, audit trails, and the principle that an admin does not see users' private conversations by default.

workflow_orchestration.title: Multi-step workflows
workflow_orchestration.body: Pre-inquiries, document drafting, document analysis, and deep research are not just one chat answer. They move through steps: mapping the situation, checking risks and sources, preparing a draft, human review, and confirmation.

domain_knowledge.title: Social-sector knowledge environment
domain_knowledge.body: The value of Sotsiaal.pro is not a generic chatbot, but a knowledge base and workflow logic built for the social sector. The platform uses information grounded in social welfare law, child protection law, municipal services, national guidance, and domain materials where sources are available.

accessibility.title: Language and accessibility
accessibility.body:
On the first visit, the Language and accessibility module opens automatically. Choose language, contrast, text size, theme, screen profile, motion and transparency, background audio and app settings.

Changes apply immediately. Reopen the same module from the hidden top control menu or from this guide; account settings are also available in Profile.

home.title: Home page and connecting to the platform
home.body:
First-visit sequence

  1. Choose settings in the Language and accessibility module.
  2. In the “Everything starts with clarity” readiness view, select Enter.
  3. Scroll through the introduction or choose Skip. Switch background audio on or off. Use the arrow next to the audio control to change tracks.
  4. In “Connect to the sotsiaal.pro platform”, press the central power button.

Cards and menus

  • Signed-out view has 9 cards: Explore features, User guide, Sign in, About, Install, Terms, Privacy policy, Pricing and Contact.
  • Side arrows move one card at a time. The bottom quick menu jumps directly to a card.
  • Focus or hover the hidden top handle to open background audio, Language and accessibility and Standby.
  • A signed-in user sees Rooms, Workspace, Chat and Profile.

register.title: Create an account and activate access
register.body:
The role is not selected on the home page. When registration is open, use Registration from the sign-in window and choose Client, Social work specialist or Service provider there. Before launch, the sign-in window may show “Registration — soon”.

  1. Enter email and a 4–8 digit PIN.
  2. Review the terms, privacy policy and guide, and give only required consents.
  3. For professional use, also review the work-use framework and organisation agreements.
  4. Confirm the email from the message sent to you.
  5. Activate a suitable plan or sponsored access. Current plans and prices are always on Pricing.

signin.title: Sign in
signin.body:
Open the Sign in card. If needed, open the email field from the envelope icon, enter email and then enter the PIN on the keypad. The arrow Enter submits sign-in. The question-mark button opens PIN recovery.

After a successful sign-in, the account navigation appears. If access needs a subscription or sponsored-period action, the platform directs you to the next required step.

chat.title: Chat
chat.body:
Chat adapts to screen width. Write a question or describe the situation in your own words; while an answer is generated, Send becomes Stop.

  • Dictation turns speech into text before sending. Review the text.
  • Voice chat opens a separate avatar view and uses the same knowledge, sources, privacy and urgent-help path as typed questions; the full answer remains in text chat.
  • Answer actions include read aloud, copy and retry. Sources appears when the answer used verifiable sources.
  • You can always ask for a simpler explanation.
  • The + next to the input opens Help request, Help offer, Deep research and Document analysis.

documents.title: Documents and files
documents.body:
Documents are available to all three roles. Clients see personal files and results; specialists and providers can also manage work files, background materials, templates, drafts and confirmed outputs.

A file added to the persistent library remains in your files. A temporary file added to Document analysis belongs to that chat workflow and does not automatically become a persistent document. Review an audio transcript separately before creating a summary.

agent_mode.title: Draft a document
agent_mode.body:
Document drafting is available to all three roles for applications, statements, letters, reports, summaries and other drafts. Choose output type, tone, language, length and template and add suitable source files.

Refine instructions in the same workspace and create versions. A person must review and confirm the draft before use; a confirmed result can be saved and downloaded as DOCX or PDF.

wellbeing.title: Work wellbeing
wellbeing.body: Work wellbeing is a private workspace for social work specialists. It includes My records, quick check, weekly and monthly overview, difficult case, workplace violence, recovery, work boundaries, interruptions, work processes, role boundaries and starter support.

profile.title: Profile and account
profile.body:
Profile brings together account and usage settings. Change PIN and email, manage subscription or sponsored access, view usage, open accessibility settings and sign out.

Account settings let you end the current or all active sessions, request a copy of your data and start account deletion. Manage sharing separately in My shares.

about.title: Public information and contact
about.body:
Home-page cards and the bottom quick menu open Features, User guide, About, Install, Terms, Privacy policy, Pricing and . The platform’s origin story is on From the author.

The hidden top menu controls background audio, track switching, accessibility and Standby. In a supported browser, Install adds Sotsiaal.pro to a phone or computer as an app.

before_use.title: Before professional use
before_use.body:
An AI answer, draft, summary or match is not an official decision. Check content, sources and context and make the substantive decision yourself.

Professional use of identifiable client or staff data requires a suitable legal and contractual basis. Review the terms, privacy policy and work-use framework. Enter only information needed for the workflow.

rooms.title: Rooms and calls
rooms.body:
Rooms are shared spaces for participants. The owner manages members, can transfer ownership and archive the room. A room can also follow a help match or an enquiry.

Voice calls are not recorded by default. Recording starts with a separate consent request and only after every required participant confirms. A confirmed meeting summary can be shared in the room and sent to participants for approval.

journey.title: Journey and preliminary enquiry
journey.body: The client Journey keeps the situation summary, related topics and next steps together. Start a preliminary enquiry from chat, a form or a blank page and submit only after your own review. My shares shows active shares and lets you withdraw them.

search.title: My search
search.body: My search searches the signed-in user’s own chats, documents and created content. It never searches another user’s material. Search on this guide page covers only the public guide text.

pro_tools.title: Workspace for three roles
pro_tools.body: The Client Workspace has 9, the Social work specialist Workspace 19 and the Service provider Workspace 19 choices. Method mirror and Work wellbeing belong to the specialist; Service log and Service profile belong to the provider. The exact list follows the role selected at the top of this page.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.body: Choose your role at the top of this guide, create the account on the registration page, confirm email and access, and sign in. Open Workspace or Chat, choose the workflow and review every draft, source and shared item before confirmation.

privacy_safety.title: Privacy warnings and urgent help
privacy_safety.body:
If the privacy pre-check notices a possible name, personal code, address, phone, email or another sensitive detail, it warns before sending.

  • Edit text leaves the text for correction.
  • Send masked replaces detected parts with labels.
  • Send anyway is available only in an allowed private workflow. Public help requests and offers use stricter minimisation.

In an urgent or dangerous situation, follow the displayed 112, Child Helpline or Victim Support guidance immediately. Sotsiaal.pro is not an emergency channel.

workspace.title: Client Workspace
workspace.body:
The Client Workspace has 9 choices.

  • Journey keeps the situation summary and next steps together.
  • Preliminary enquiry helps prepare an enquiry before submission.
  • Help requests and Help offers support asking for or offering help.
  • Invite participant opens an invitation.
  • Service map helps find services, contacts and published help information.
  • My search searches only your own content.
  • Draft a document helps create an application, statement or other draft.
  • My shares shows what you shared and lets you withdraw it.

workflows.title: Key client workflows
workflows.body:
Start in Chat or Journey when you need an explanation and next steps. A preliminary enquiry can start from a chat summary, a form or a blank page; nothing is submitted before you confirm it.

Review the text and privacy warning before publishing a help request or offer. A match can open a shared room. Continue with the Service map, document drafting or My shares when you are ready for a concrete action.

quickstart.title: Start as a client
quickstart.body:
1. Choose Client when creating the account and confirm your email.
  2. Sign in with email and PIN.
  3. Open Chat or Workspace and choose Journey, Preliminary enquiry or another workflow.
  4. Describe the situation in your own words; ask for a simpler explanation when needed.
  5. Check the sources when the answer includes a Sources button.
  6. Always review a draft or shared information before confirming it.

workspace.title: Social work specialist Workspace
workspace.body:
The Social work specialist Workspace has 19 choices.

Enquiries · Help requests · Help offers · Invite participant · Fieldwork · My cases · Casework desk · Service map · My search · Materials · Draft a document · Documents · Supervision · Mentoring · Covision · Method mirror · Work wellbeing · Organisations · My shares.

Method mirror and Work wellbeing belong to the specialist tools; Service log and Service profile belong to the service provider Workspace.

workflows.title: Specialist case and work workflows
workflows.body:
• Enquiries brings together incoming enquiries and intake.
  • My cases keeps core case information and links together; Casework desk brings together daily preparation, meetings, drafts and next steps.
  • Fieldwork, Documents and Draft a document support preparation, notes and confirmed outputs.
  • Covision, Supervision, Mentoring, Method mirror and Work wellbeing support professional reflection and resilience.
  • Materials submits knowledge-base additions; Organisations opens the organisation workspace.

quickstart.title: Start as a social work specialist
quickstart.body:
1. Choose Social work specialist when creating the account and confirm your email.
  2. Before using identifiable client data professionally, check organisation agreements and the work-use framework.
  3. Sign in and open Workspace.
  4. Start with Enquiries, My cases or Casework desk; use Chat for a general question.
  5. Use only necessary information and respond to privacy warnings.
  6. Review AI text, summaries and sources before professional use.

workspace.title: Service provider Workspace
workspace.body:
The Service provider Workspace has 19 choices.

Enquiries · Help requests · Help offers · Invite participant · Fieldwork · Service log · My cases · Casework desk · Service map · My search · Materials · Draft a document · Documents · Service profile · Supervision · Mentoring · Covision · Organisations · My shares.

Service log and Service profile belong to provider tools. Method mirror and Work wellbeing belong to the social work specialist Workspace.

workflows.title: Service-delivery workflows
workflows.body:
• Enquiries and help workflows support intake and matching people.
  • Service profile manages public organisation, service, location, target-group, price, waiting-time and contact information.
  • Service log brings together delivered work, visits, corrections, monthly views, reports and exports with a controlled history.
  • My cases, Casework desk, Fieldwork and document work support daily service delivery.
  • Organisations opens member, intake, schedule, reporting, funding, audit and settings views.

quickstart.title: Start as a service provider
quickstart.body:
1. Choose Service provider when creating the account and confirm your email.
  2. Join an organisation through an invitation or set up your organisation workspace.
  3. Complete the Service profile so services are findable on the Service map.
  4. Use Enquiries for intake and Service log for delivered work.
  5. Check documents, summaries, reports and public service information before confirming or publishing them.

1.title: Presence and agreements
1.lead: We confirm roles, confidentiality and the case boundary before opening substantive work.
1.hero: The case owner confirms that the shared picture is accurate and sufficiently anonymous.

2.title: Building the case picture
2.lead: We collect facts, perspectives and professional tensions on separate cards.
2.hero: One active anchor keeps the centre of the story visible. Supporting cards clarify rather than compete.

3.title: Exploratory questions
3.lead: We prepare questions privately and share them one at a time to broaden the case picture.
3.hero: Only one question is central at a time. Its answer may change the shared picture.

4.title: Reflection circle
4.lead: Participants share observations and possible meanings; the case owner does not have to decide yet.
4.hero: A reflection is a tentative perspective, not a diagnosis or solution.

5.title: Creating possibilities
5.lead: We create possibilities in different directions without voting, ranking or immediate feasibility scoring.
5.hero: One possibility is central; others wait visibly for their turn to be shared.

6.title: Resources and conditions
6.eyebrow: What can genuinely support this direction?
6.lead: We connect possibilities with resources, supporting conditions, limits and critical prerequisites.
6.hero: The resource picture does not assess a person. It shows influence, support and what needs agreement.

7.title: Direction and first step
7.lead: The case owner defines the chosen direction, a first step within their influence and an honest follow-up.
7.hero: The group does not vote. The owner decides and shares only the confirmed summary.

8.title: Learning and handover
8.lead: We confirm the owner package, follow-up, group learning and retention decisions.
8.hero: The final review prepares an immutable output. The session leader closes the case only through the final gate.

help.section_usage_controls: Package limits and per-user exceptions. Saving does not edit the current package: it creates a new version and moves active subscriptions onto it. Soft limit warns, hard limit stops. An override is one user's temporary exception, not a package change.
help.section_deletion_jobs: Background deletion and cleanup jobs. Active shows queued and running ones; a FAILED row stays here with its error code until someone re-runs it. A long-standing queue means deletion requests are not completing.
help.section_notifications: Notifications whose email delivery failed. Each row shows status, type and the last error code. Requeue puts the message back in the send queue. A repeating error code across rows points at the mail service, not at one message.
help.section_platform: The platform's four workflows at a glance: chat and voice, help flow, rooms and invites, documents and agent. Figures cover 30 days unless stated otherwise.
help.section_storage: Server-side file usage across the paths the app tracks. Free disk space is the whole volume, not an app quota; when it nears zero, file uploads stop first.
help.section_framework_acceptances: Work-framework acceptances: who confirmed the framework at registration and who also took the signed agreement. Accepted but not downloaded means the user does not have the document.
help.section_rag_docs: State and quality of the RAG knowledge base. The top part is the overview; below are two work queues, each with its own info button. Start with the high-risk queue: those sources already reached users.
help.section_billing: Subscriptions and payments over 30 days. The second row is the payment chain: initiated to checkout to webhook. A sharp drop between checkout and paid points at the payment integration.
help.section_users: User usage, cost and limits. This section also holds the bulk actions (send email, delete accounts); both require a reason, a written confirmation and show an impact preview first. Deletion cannot be undone.
help.section_ai_costs: AI cost observability from ChatLog: usage units, approximate euro cost, attribution completeness and budget thresholds. The unit is an internal normalised measure, not a provider invoice.
help.section_logs: The event log with filters, plus log deletion. Deletion affects exactly the rows the filter currently shows: check the filter before you press. It needs a reason and a written confirmation, and cannot be undone.
help.section_reset: Prelaunch reset: targeted cleanup actions before going live. Every action shows an impact preview first and needs a written confirmation. Execution is disabled in production; there you only get the preview.
help.framework_acceptances: Recent work-framework acceptances captured at registration. Check that new sign-ups appear here; a missing framework download means the user has not taken the signed agreement.
help.high_risk_sources: Sources that reached a high-risk answer or the displayed-source panel while their freshness is stale, missing or unknown. Work top-down: every row here is a source a user may already have seen.
help.quality_queue: Source metadata, freshness, URL, form and contact gaps from the latest audited RAG documents, most severe first. The Fix column names the exact action and target.
help.rag_recent: The most recently indexed RAG documents. Use it to confirm that an ingest actually landed and finished; FAILED rows need re-ingestion.
help.payments: The latest 20 payment attempts across all time. Repeated FAILED rows from one provider point at a payment integration problem, not at the user.
help.users: Per-user 30 day usage, budget-model cost estimate and active limits. The bars show how much of the limit is used: amber from 75%, red from 90%.
help.ai_features: AI usage units by route and stage. Direct means measured usage, estimated means derived from the unit model; low coverage means the numbers understate real use.
help.ai_users: Users who have reached at least 85% of their monthly budget. These are the accounts to review before the limit stops them mid-work.
help.ai_packages: Budget tracking per package: how much of the package budget the active subscriptions have consumed.
help.logs: The latest events with filters. Meta holds the machine-readable detail of the event; use the filters to isolate one event type or crisis flags.
