voimalused.title: Sotsiaal.pro features
voimalused.intro: This is a complete overview of Sotsiaal.pro services and tools. Each feature explains who it is for and what it enables; exact access depends on the user's role and plan.
voimalused.s1_body: For all three roles. In chat you can describe a situation in your own words, ask about services, benefits, rights, or professional practice, and ask for a simpler explanation. Sotsiaal.pro adapts its response style to the user's role, helps organise the issue, and suggests next steps; decisions always remain with people. The Sources action appears when a response uses verifiable sources.
voimalused.s2_body: Sotsiaal.pro answers draw on the platform knowledge base, which brings together social-sector legislation, guidance, methods, local-government information and forms. When an answer uses sources, you can open the materials and verify where the information came from. The knowledge base is maintained and professional submissions are added after review.
voimalused.s3_body: Your steps stay together on the Journey: a summary of what has happened, related topics, missing information and next steps. The Journey is private. You decide whether and with whom to share it; sharing happens with your confirmation, and you can review and revoke your shares in the My shares view.
voimalused.s4_body: Before a message is sent, the privacy pre-layer notices unnecessary personal data and offers to remove it. Sharing always happens with your confirmation. If the situation described is urgent, we show the right contacts right away — 112, Lasteabi and Ohvriabi.
voimalused.s5_body: The Client Workspace has 9 choices: Journey, Preliminary enquiry, Help requests, Help offers, Invite participant, Service map, My search, Draft a document and My shares. The Social work specialist Workspace has 19 choices: Enquiries, Help requests, Help offers, Invite participant, Fieldwork, My cases, Casework desk, Service map, My search, Materials, Draft a document, Documents, Supervision, Mentoring, Covision, Method mirror, Work wellbeing, Organisations and My shares. The Service provider Workspace has 19 choices: Enquiries, Help requests, Help offers, Invite participant, Fieldwork, Service log, My cases, Casework desk, Service map, My search, Materials, Draft a document, Documents, Service profile, Supervision, Mentoring, Covision, Organisations and My shares.
voimalused.s6_body: A pre-inquiry helps you think an inquiry through before submitting it. You can start in three ways: continuing from a chat where a summary already exists, filling in a form, or from a blank page. The summary and draft take shape together with you — you submit only once you have reviewed everything yourself. The inquiry reaches the recipient's Workspace, and if needed a shared chat room can be opened with the parties.
voimalused.s7_body: Describe what support you need, or offer what you can give. The platform helps match them, and when a match is made, a shared chat room opens for agreeing on next steps. Published help requests and help offers are also visible on the Service Map.
voimalused.s8_body: For all roles. A room lets a help seeker, social work professional, service provider, or colleague communicate together. The owner manages members, can transfer ownership, and archive the room. Voice calls are not recorded by default; recording starts only after a separate consent request and approval by every required participant. An approved meeting summary can be shared and sent to participants for confirmation.
voimalused.s9_body: When you need an application, a statement or another document, describe what you need — the draft takes shape together with you based on your description, and you review it before use. The finished document stays in your files.
voimalused.s10_body: For all three roles. Help seekers see their personal files and results; social work professionals and service providers can also manage work files, background materials, templates, drafts, and approved outputs. A file can be assigned a role, used in document drafting, and an approved result downloaded as DOCX or PDF. A temporary file added to chat for analysis does not automatically enter the persistent library.
voimalused.s11_body: Specialists can discuss cases in co-vision: a shared case canvas keeps the discussion focused and the conclusions together, and best practices remain for the future. Colleagues' support is there even when people are in different places.
voimalused.s12_body: For social work professionals. The Wellbeing area includes My records, a quick check, weekly and monthly overview, difficult case, workplace violence, recovery, work boundaries, interruptions, work processes, role boundaries, and starter support. Records help identify strain and choose a small next step; personal wellbeing information is not shared with others by default.
voimalused.s13_body: A specialist can submit guidance, methodologies and practical materials to enrich the Sotsiaal.pro knowledge base. Material reaches the database after review. This way the environment grows together with the field's practice.
voimalused.s14_body: For all roles. The Service map helps find municipal social-service contacts, service providers, services, service locations, and published help requests and offers. Search by name, description, service, category, target group, address, or area.
voimalused.s15_body: Professional supervision supports the specialist: the process runs under a package agreed with the supervisor, and meetings, agreements, and outputs stay together on the platform. The outputs remain yours after the process ends.
voimalused.s16_body: Mentoring supports specialists who are starting out: the agreements and meetings of the mentoring relationship stay together in the mentor's and mentee's shared view.
voimalused.s17_body: The field work view is built for use on the move: visit preparation, notes, and the summary stay together even when the work happens outside the office.
voimalused.s18_body: When signed in, you can search your own content — conversations, documents, and other things you have created — from one place. The search shows only your own materials, never anyone else's.
voimalused.s19_body: The method mirror is the specialist's private reflection tool: after a case, you can briefly note what worked and what to do differently next time. Entries are visible only to you.
voimalused.group_roles_body: The Workspace brings together the services and tools relevant to each person's role.
voimalused.group_core_body: These features support asking questions, checking information, and working with your own materials.
voimalused.group_client_body: A help seeker can make sense of a situation, find support, and decide what to do or share next.
voimalused.group_collaboration_body: Document work and shared rooms help people prepare, share, and approve results they have chosen themselves.
voimalused.group_professional_title: Tools for professionals and service providers
voimalused.group_professional_body: Professional tools support case work, service delivery, wellbeing, and learning with colleagues.
voimalused.group_account_body: These features support organisational work, account management, accessibility, and user rights.
voimalused.group_admin_body: Administrator tools help keep services, sources, access, and platform health under control.
voimalused.s20_body: For all roles. Dictation turns speech into editable text before sending. A separate avatar-based voice chat transcribes each turn and uses the same knowledge, sources, privacy, and safety path as text chat; a short answer is spoken while the full answer and available sources remain in chat. Responses can also be read aloud in the regular view.
voimalused.s21_body: For all roles. Deep research creates a more detailed, source-based overview of a social topic, service, law, guide, or practical question. It highlights findings, connections, gaps, and next steps, and completed research remains available to the user.
voimalused.s22_body: For all roles. Add a file to chat, ask about its contents, and find important passages, explanations, or summaries. By default the analysis focuses on the uploaded document; Sotsiaal.pro domain context can be added when needed. A temporary analysis file does not automatically become a persistent document.
voimalused.s23_body: For all roles. When a response uses sources, the source panel lets you inspect the law, guide, municipal page, service information, article, or other material used. Users can report an inaccurate or outdated source for review.
voimalused.s24_body: For all roles. My shares is the user's privacy control centre: it shows which Journey, case, or other workflow information has been shared and with whom, and lets the user revoke an active share. Sharing never happens without a deliberate action and confirmation.
voimalused.s25_body: For all roles. A user can invite a help seeker, professional, service provider, or colleague to a room and, when needed, sponsor the invitee's role-based access. The notification centre gathers important invites, replies, approvals, and workflow changes, while the Workspace helps continue unfinished work.
voimalused.s26_body: For social work professionals and service providers. My cases gathers the case's core information, relationships, work items, and retention. The Case workbench provides a daily view of preparations, missing information, meetings, tasks, drafts, and next steps. AI can assist preparation but does not make official decisions or transfer information to another system without human review.
voimalused.s27_body: For service providers. The Service log records work performed, visits, service entries, and summaries, with controlled correction and cancellation history. Day and month views, a client view, reports, sharing, and export help reporting emerge as a by-product of real work.
voimalused.s28_body: For social work professionals and service providers. The organisation workspace includes overview, structure, members and invites, intake, schedule and daily route, service profile, staff support, Service log reports, funding and billing, audit, settings, and owner data export. People join through an invitation and access is role-based.
voimalused.s29_title: Topic seeds, completed cases, and best practices
voimalused.s29_body: For social work professionals and service providers. A topic seed brings a recurring observation into covision or a learning queue. Completed cases keep follow-up and learning together. Best practices turn a successful approach into a generalised entry, pass anonymity and quality review, and make an approved practice discoverable to others.
voimalused.s30_body: For clients and urgent-help desk members. A regional urgent-help desk lets a client submit a structured request and follow its progress. A desk member can accept, hand over, resolve or route it into the ordinary workflow. This service does not replace 112, Child Helpline or Victim Support crisis channels.
voimalused.s31_body: For help seekers. The tool uses entered household, housing-cost, and income information to make a preliminary browser-based estimate and explain what may be needed for an official application. The result is an estimate, not a municipal decision.
voimalused.s32_body: For service providers. A Service profile manages organisation details, contacts, accessibility, service area and locations, plus each service's target group, price, availability, waiting time, referral requirements, and contact routes. Published information makes the service discoverable on the Service map and in Sotsiaal.pro recommendations.
voimalused.s33_body: For all roles. Profile lets users change PIN and email, manage a subscription or sponsored access, view usage, sign out, and open language and accessibility settings. Users can adjust language, text size, contrast, screen profile, motion, and transparency, and install Sotsiaal.pro as an app on a phone or computer.
voimalused.s34_title: Sessions, data copy, and account deletion
voimalused.s34_body: For all roles. Users can end the current or all active sessions, request a copy of their data, and start account deletion. Export and deletion follow role, ownership, sharing, and retention boundaries so another person's or organisation's content is not included.
voimalused.s35_body: For administrators. Administration views bring together knowledge-base health and self-checks, source packages, documents, content ingestion, municipal and organisation sources, source feedback and service freshness. meist.title: About us
meist.meta_description: Sotsiaal.pro is a digital environment for the social field: clarity by asking, AI support and practical tools — decisions always stay with people.
meist.intro1a: When life gets hard — a job is lost, strength runs out, a loved one needs care — the first obstacle is usually not the absence of help. The first obstacle is not knowing: what can I even ask for, from whom, and in what words? The answers exist in laws, agencies and registers, but they are written in the language of the system, not of people. The field's own
meist.intro1b: says the same: finding your way between services, benefits and contacts takes time that is often not there. And worry does not watch the clock — the hardest questions tend to come when no office is open.
meist.intro2: Sotsiaal.pro is an Estonian platform built for exactly that gap. In one place you find trustworthy information, AI support, practical tools and communication — for a person seeking clarity, for a specialist doing social work, and for an organisation providing services. Our principle is simple: clarity should come from asking, not searching. You describe your situation in your own words — in Estonian, Russian or English — and get an answer in plain language, always with its sources.
meist.h_never: Three things we will never do
meist.never_intro: Artificial intelligence raises fair questions in the social field. We answer them with three firm promises.
meist.never1_title: A machine will never decide about you.
meist.never1_body: No benefit, service or assessment is ever born here as an algorithm's decision. AI explains, puts thoughts in order and prepares the ground — the decision is always made by a person with the right and the responsibility to make it. We do not calculate risk scores and we do not predict anyone's life.
meist.never2_body: The heart of social work is meeting, listening and trust — a machine does not do that. Our job is to take away everything else: searching, typing, entering the same thing twice. So that people have time for people.
meist.never3_body: Your conversations do not travel behind your back. Asking for help here is as private as the worry itself: you decide what to share, with whom and when, and you can withdraw any sharing. Your story stays yours even if a paid plan ends — you can always get a copy of your data.
meist.who1_body: At any hour you can describe your situation and ask which benefits and services exist, what they mean and where to turn next. A large, tangled worry becomes a few clear steps. And if the situation is urgent, we show right away where to really turn.
meist.who2_body: The Workspace helps you prepare for meetings, document less and listen more. Co-vision, supervision and wellbeing tools are a natural part of work here, not a luxury — because a supported specialist is the foundation of strong social work. What you note about your own wellbeing stays yours alone.
meist.who3_body: Your work deserves visibility and dignity: a service profile and presence on the map, responding to help requests, and meeting summaries in one place. Our aim is for paperwork to keep shrinking — reporting should be born as a by-product of real work, not as an evening's extra shift.
meist.success_body: Most digital services measure success by how long they can keep you. We measure the opposite: how quickly you get back to your life. Our success is when you reach clarity, get help from the right place — and need us a little less each time.
meist.we_body: Sotsiaal.pro is a social impact company built in Estonia: our goal is public good, and revenue serves that goal. We develop the platform deliberately and step by step, together with people from the field.

info.title: Service log
info.what_entry: Mark the service where the work ends — not from memory in the evening. One entry is a client, a service, a date and a quantity.
info.what_output: At the end of the month the same entries produce both the timesheet (the invoice basis) and the draft of the narrative report. You enter once, the outputs are many.
info.what_units: If you mark the arrival and departure times, the system works out the duration itself. The unit comes with the service or the referral; if there are several, you are asked which one.
info.what_field: If the visit started in Field work, closing it gives you a prefilled entry: date, times and duration are already in place.
info.day_title: The day: one button at a time
info.day_flow: There is one button at a time, and its label says what comes next: “I have arrived”, then “I left”. Above the button you can see where you are — for example “On site since 10:12”. Once the visit is marked, you save the entry with a separate button.
info.day_travel: Counting travel time can only be chosen before you start. The sequence then gains “Starting travel” at the front and “I am back” at the end. After the first mark the choice locks, because a step added afterwards would have no time to record.
info.day_undo: A wrong tap is not final: “Correct the last mark” removes the most recent stamp.
info.day_offline: No signal does not stop the work. The entry is stored on the device and sends itself once the network returns; the screen shows how many entries are waiting.
info.day_no_double: Resending does not create a duplicate. Every entry carries its own key and the server recognises the same entry even if the reply was lost.
info.referral_what: A referral is the municipality's decision: for whom, which service, how much and for how long. An entry is linked to a referral and takes its unit and recipient from there.
info.referral_saldo: The balance is visible throughout. When the volume is running out the system warns you — but does not block the entry: undocumented work is worse than work documented over the allocation.
info.referral_lock: Once a referral has entries, its unit, recipient and decision number can no longer be changed. Otherwise the basis on which an invoice was already issued would change after the fact.
info.report_deadline: The report usually goes to the municipality by the 10th of the following month. One gentle reminder arrives on the 5th — no more than that.
info.report_finalize: An entry is born as a draft. Exports leave drafts out by default, so confirm the month's entries before building the report — otherwise the file may come out empty.
info.report_templates: The four templates — timesheet, care diary, narrative report and statistics extract — are not filled in separately. All four come from the same entries.
info.report_multi_kov: When you serve several municipalities, choose the recipient: each one gets only its own rows. A file built without a recipient carries a warning that it must not be submitted to any municipality.
info.report_formats: The format is your choice: CSV for a spreadsheet, Word for editing, PDF for signing. PDF does not support Cyrillic — if a client's name is in Cyrillic, choose Word.
info.narrative_what: The narrative report is a story, not a number: goals, what was done, progress, obstacles and finally a proposal — continue, change the volume, or end.
info.narrative_seed: The summary is already waiting: volumes, activities and notes together with their provenance. You write them out.
info.narrative_ai: If you want, the AI drafts from that same summary. It is marked as a draft and stays one until you read it, correct it and save it — the responsibility is yours, not the machine's.
info.narrative_provenance: Provenance does not melt together: what the client said, what you observed and what a document states stay distinguishable in the report. That distinction is what makes the report trustworthy.
info.confirm_manual: For an external client's paper signature you can put a mark on the entry. It is a record of a signature, not the signature itself.
info.confirm_client: A platform client can confirm their own month when this view is open. The confirmation is final and cannot be withdrawn later — a dispute belongs between people, not under a button.
info.confirm_client_sees: The client sees only confirmed entries: date, quantity and the provider's name. They do not see your note.
info.privacy_note: The note is a short factual mark for the report, not a case story. Sensitive content, diagnoses and third parties' data do not belong here.
info.privacy_retention: A service entry is an invoice source document and is kept for 7 years. The period starts at the end of the financial year in which the entry was recorded. A mistaken entry is corrected with a reason or voided — never quietly overwritten.
info.privacy_location: Location is not stored by default. If it is switched on, a single point is requested at the moment you tap “I have arrived”, and you are shown whether it was stored. A continuous location trail is never collected, and refusing permission does not prevent the timestamp.
info.privacy_measure: The system measures how long MAKING THE ENTRY takes — not the service. That number is yours, nobody else sees it, and it is used to make the tool faster, not to judge your pace of work.

trail.author_only_note: These are your follow-ups. The care coordinator's notes are not shown here.

chronology.title: Client chronology
chronology.intro: Choose a period and review the entries. Only the entries you select go into the document, and you can remove third-party details from the text. The diary entries are not changed.
chronology.empty: There are no entries in this period.
chronology.restricted: coordinator only; left out by default
chronology.requester_hint: For example the authority and the official's name.
chronology.basis_hint: For example the request number and the legal basis.
chronology.registry_ref: Reference in the organisation's document register (optional)
chronology.created: The document has been compiled and added to the release log.
chronology.print_hint: The document opens in a new tab. To get a PDF, choose “Print” in the browser and “Save as PDF” as the destination.

doc.title: Client chronology
doc.redacted: the compiler has shortened the text for release
doc.privacy_note: This document contains special categories of personal data. It may be used only for the purpose it was released for.
doc.scope_note: The document holds the entries the compiler selected from the client's home care diary for the stated period; it may not be the whole diary.
doc.print_hint: To get a PDF, choose “Print” in the browser and “Save as PDF” as the destination. This line is not printed.

releases.title: Release log
releases.intro: Every compiled chronology: for whom, on what basis and who compiled it. The official register is the organisation's document management; this list is a work log.

outbox.title: Entries waiting on this device: {count}
outbox.hint: These entries are only on this device (encrypted) and will be sent when the connection returns. Do not clear the browser's data before they are sent.
outbox.attention_hint: The server did not accept this entry. The text is kept here: copy it, write the entry again on the client's page and then delete it from here.
outbox.delete_confirm: Delete for good, the entry will be lost
outbox.unreadable: This entry can no longer be opened on this device
outbox.full: There are already {limit} unsent entries on this device. Restore the connection and send them first.
outbox.blocked_hint: You do not have access to this client's diary right now. Open the client's page (as a covering worker, choose a reason) or talk to the care coordinator. The entry stays on this device and will be sent when access returns.

dictation.listening: Listening. When you are done, press “Stop and add the text”.
dictation.hint: Speech is turned into text by the platform's speech recognition and added to the end of the field; the recording is not kept. Read the text before saving.
dictation.cut: The entry's length limit ({limit} characters) was reached and the end of the dictated text was left out. Save this entry and continue in a new one.

import.title: Import clients from a table
import.intro: Copy the client table (for example from a spreadsheet) and paste it here, or choose a CSV file. Each row is one client. Before importing you see what becomes of each row.
import.columns_hint: The first row must hold the column names. Recognised: Name (required), Code, Address, Phone, Note. Up to {limit} rows at a time.
import.text_hint: The code is the organisation's own mark (for example the same name as in another system). A client with a code is not imported a second time.
import.file_label: or choose a file (CSV or text)
import.file_encoding: The file has characters that could not be read (accented letters are broken). Save the file as UTF-8 or copy the table and paste it into the field above.
import.file_failed: The file could not be read.
import.count_repeated: Same code a second time in the table: {count}
import.count_same_name: A client with the same name already exists: {count}
import.confirm_same_name: This is another person: import anyway
import.done: Clients imported: {count}. Add teams and cards on each client's page.

history.title: Earlier history from another place
history.empty: If a diary about this client has been kept elsewhere (for example in Drive), it can be imported here.
history.mark: imported history, authors and times not verified
history.remove_confirm: Remove from here, the original stays
history.add_hint: Copy the client's existing diary and paste it here, or choose a text file. The text is imported as it is: no entries are made from it and no dates are derived. Check that it is the right client's diary.
history.hits_hint: These passages are from imported text; the kind and period filters do not apply to them.
history.hits_more: There are more matches. Narrow the search.

door_tag.title: Door tag
door_tag.intro: The tag goes inside the client's home, next to the door. The worker scans the code with the phone camera and lands on this client's page.
door_tag.safe: The tag does not give access: the address holds a random mark from which no name can be read, and the client's page opens only for a signed-in worker who can see this client.
door_tag.qr_label: QR code of the door tag
door_tag.print_hint: The tag opens in a new tab. Print it and cut it out along the dashed line; the client's name is not on the tag.
door_tag.nfc_hint: The same address can be written to an NFC sticker: then it is enough to hold the phone against the sticker.
door_tag.none: This client has no door tag yet.
door_tag.replace_confirm: Make a new tag, the current one stops working
door_tag.revoke_confirm: Cancel the tag, it stops working

doc.title: Door tag
doc.print_hint: Print this page and cut the tag out along the dashed line. This line is not printed.
doc.what: Home care worker: scan the code with the phone camera.
doc.safe: The code opens nobody's data without signing in.

call.open: Call: the client or a relative called
call.note_hint: Without an explanation the diary gets the caller and the topic.
call.saved: The call note is in the diary.

calls.title: Call counter
calls.intro: What people call about and who calls, month by month. The counter counts the call notes workers make on the client page; only numbers are shown here.
calls.empty: No call notes were made in this or the previous month.
calls.how: A worker makes a call note on the client page with the button “Call: the client or a relative called”. Retracted entries are not counted.

export.title: Complete export
export.intro: All home care data in one file: for a backup, at a supervisor's request or to move to another system. The file is in JSON format and other software can read it.
export.who_hint: Only the coordinator of the whole organisation can make an export. Every export leaves a row in the organisation's work log: who, when and why.
export.contents_more: The file also holds teams, card lines, the trail of corrections and retractions, read marks, incident follow-ups, the trail of door tags, staff names and the home care work log.
export.excluded_title: What is not in the file

excluded.entry_search_helpers: Search helpers (word stems and base forms): they are derived from the entry text and the text itself is in the file.
excluded.request_keys: Repeat-send keys: a technical guard against saving twice.
excluded.door_tag_marks: Door tag marks: a mark is a working address. The file holds the trail of making and cancelling a tag.
excluded.device_queue: Entries still waiting for a connection on a worker's device: they have not reached the server.
excluded.user_accounts: Staff e-mail addresses and sign-in data. The file holds only the names of staff that home care rows refer to.
excluded.service_diary: Service diary billing entries: a separate function with its own export.

reasons.LEAVING: leaving or moving to another system

export.reason_hint: The reason goes to the organisation's work log with your name, the time and the file's checksum.
export.confirm_notice: The file holds the names, addresses and diaries of all clients. Save it only where client files may be kept and do not send it by e-mail.
export.working: Making the export. This can take up to a couple of minutes; do not close the page.
export.ready: The export is ready: {rows} rows, {size}. If the download did not start by itself, press "Save file".
export.checksum_hint: The browser recomputed the file's checksum and it matches the server's. The same sum is in the organisation's work log: to prove later that the file is unchanged, compute the file's SHA-256 and compare.
export.not_verified: The browser could not recompute the file's checksum; the size matches. Compute the file's SHA-256 yourself and compare it with the sum above before you rely on the file.
export.mismatch: The downloaded file does not match the server's data (size or checksum). The file was not offered for saving; try again.
export.recent_empty: No export has been made yet.

activities.title: Activities
activities.intro: The organisation's activities in its own words. Each activity belongs to one group of the regulation; the care plan, the visit record and the report will use the same activities.
activities.empty: No activities have been added yet.
activities.empty_editor: No activities have been added yet. You can start from the 16 groups of the regulation and then rename the activities in your own words.
activities.seed: Add the regulation's 16 groups as a starting list

groups.HEATING: Ordering and storing heating material, and heating
groups.HOME_SAFETY: Watching the safety of the home and keeping the living environment safe
groups.HOUSEKEEPING: Tidying the home, keeping the yard and following upkeep rules
groups.HYGIENE: Personal hygiene, using the toilet and incontinence aids
groups.LAUNDRY: Changing bed linen and doing laundry
groups.MEDICATION: Taking medicines and watching the state of health as instructed by a health worker
groups.ABILITY_MONITORING: Watching functional ability during the service
groups.NETWORK: Keeping contact with close ones and encouraging taking part in community life
groups.MENTAL_SUPPORT: Getting mental health and spiritual support

activities.group_empty: This group has no activities yet.
activities.name: Name of the activity
activities.note: Note for the care worker (you may leave this empty)
activities.source: The groups come from regulation no 40 of the Minister of Social Protection of 29.06.2023, "Requirements for home care" (§ 2).

plan.title: Care plan
plan.none: No care plan is in force yet.
plan.editor_intro: You are changing a draft. The plan in force stays the same until you put the draft into force; the earlier plan then stays in the list of earlier plans.
plan.none_yet: This client has no care plan in force yet.
plan.catalogue_empty: The organisation's catalogue of activities is empty. Plan lines are chosen from the catalogue: add the activities first.
plan.goals_label: Goals of the service for the client (write them down together with the client)
plan.frequency_note: When exactly (you may leave this empty)
plan.line_note: Note on this activity (you may leave this empty)
plan.note_label: Note on the whole plan (you may leave this empty)
plan.draft_saved: The draft is saved. The plan in force has not changed.
plan.activate_confirm: Confirm: this plan comes into force
plan.activate_confirm_replace: Confirm: this replaces the plan in force
plan.activated: The plan is in force. The team sees it on the client's page.
plan.draft_discarded: The draft is discarded. The plan in force did not change.

decision.title: Decision and volume
decision.none: No decision in force is on record.
decision.period_open: in force from {from}, no end date
decision.editor_intro: Write down what the municipality has decided: who decided, until when the decision is in force and how much help it grants. The decision document stays where it is now.
decision.none_yet: No decisions are on record yet.
decision.number_label: Number of the decision or contract
decision.until_hint: Leave empty if the decision has no end date.
decision.until_clear: Remove the end: the decision has no end date
decision.hours_hint: For example 6 or 6.5. Leave empty if the decision states no hours.
decision.period_label: The period the volume is for
decision.fee_hint: In your own words, for example "free of charge" or "own contribution 2 euros an hour".
decision.retract_confirm: Confirm: the decision was entered by mistake
decision.retracted_notice: The decision is retracted. It stays visible here.

deadlines.title: Deadlines
deadlines.intro: Decisions and care plans that need your attention. Clients receiving the service and clients temporarily away are counted (now {count}).
deadlines.truncated: The first {count} clients by name were counted.
deadlines.decisions_ending_empty: No client's decision ends within 60 days.
deadlines.no_decision_empty: Every client has a decision in force.
deadlines.plans_due_title: Care plan is due for review
deadlines.plans_due_empty: No care plan's review day has passed or falls within 30 days.
deadlines.no_plan_empty: Every client has a care plan in force.
deadlines.work_nature_due_title: Work marks that need a review
deadlines.work_nature_due_empty: No mark is due for review within 30 days.
deadlines.money_open_title: Client's money held by a worker for over a week
deadlines.money_open_empty: No balance has been open for over a week.
deadlines.feedback_hint: Feedback is asked regularly and when a service ends, from relatives too. Write it into the client's diary as an incident of the kind feedback, thanks or complaint.
deadlines.feedback_overdue_title: No feedback asked for over a year
deadlines.feedback_overdue_empty: Feedback has been asked from every client within a year.
deadlines.feedback_at_end_empty: Feedback is recorded for the services that ended in the last three months.
deadlines.supplies_open_title: Supplies running low or run out
deadlines.supplies_open_empty: No followed supply is running low.
deadlines.away_long_empty: Nobody has been away for over a month.
deadlines.changes_open_title: Noticed changes waiting for an answer
deadlines.changes_open_empty: No noticed change is waiting for an answer.

visit.title: What you did
visit.no_plan: There is no care plan in force. You can add an activity from the organisation's catalogue.
visit.other_placeholder: Choose an activity from the catalogue
visit.catalogue_done: All activities of the catalogue are already in the list.
visit.minutes_label: Length of the visit in minutes (may be left empty)
visit.text_optional: If the visit went as usual, the text may stay empty. Write if you noticed something new.
visit.reason_missing: Choose why the activity was not done, or remove the mark.

month.title: Month summary
month.intro: Visit records by month: provided time next to the decided volume, the workers' time and missed visits. Entries that are not retracted and have a length or done activities are counted.
month.totals: In total: {visits} visits, time {amount}; length not marked on {without} visits; {missed} missed visits.
month.until_today: Current month: the decided time is counted up to today ({date}).
month.clients_empty: There are no clients in this view.
month.expected_none: no decided volume for this period
month.workers_empty: There are no visit records in this month.
month.missed_empty: No missed visits are on record for this month.
month.how: The incidents "did not open the door" and "refused help" are counted as missed visits. When two workers were on a visit, the client's time is counted once and each worker gets it. There are no kilometres here: the home care diary does not measure trips.
month.not_done: activities not done: refused {refused}, not needed {notNeeded}, could not be done {couldNot}

slots.title: Visits in a week
slots.none: No recurring visits are on record.
slots.worker_inactive: the worker's membership is not valid
slots.editor_intro: Recurring visits at this client's home. A change applies from today; the plan of past days stays as it was.
slots.edit_hint: The change applies from today. For another weekday end this visit and add a new one.
slots.team_empty: There is nobody on the client's team to assign a visit to. Add a worker to the team on the client's page.
slots.end_confirm: Confirm: from today this visit is no longer planned
slots.ended: The visit is ended. The plan of past days was kept.

day.title: Day plan
day.intro: The pattern of visits with this day's changes. A visit is done when the client has a visit record that day; it is not ticked here by hand.
day.week_day: {weekday} {date}: {planned} visits, {unassigned} not assigned, {missing} without a record, {uncovered} with the worker absent
day.totals: {planned} visits, planned time {amount}. Done {done}, no record {missing}, cancelled {cancelled}, not assigned {unassigned}, worker absent {uncovered}.
day.empty: No visits are planned for this day.
day.away_hint: The pattern holds, but the visit is not made while the client is away.

cancel_reasons.CLIENT_AWAY: the client is not at home
cancel_reasons.WORKER_ABSENT: the worker is absent, no replacement found

day.saved: The day plan is changed. The pattern of visits stayed the same.
day.uncovered_hint: These visits need a replacement or a decision. The more important ones come first.
day.obstacles_hint: Reported by the care worker. Their visits not yet done are in order of importance: move or cancel them, then mark the notice as seen.
day.obstacle_none: This worker has no visits left to do on this day.
day.obstacle_absent: Mark an absence for this day
day.obstacle_handled_saved: The notice is marked as seen.
day.obstacle_absent_saved: The absence is marked. The worker's visits not yet done are in the group “Worker absent”.

priority.label: Importance of the visit
priority.hint: Importance says what must happen even when fewer workers are at work.
priority.B: B: may shift within the day
priority.C: C: may shift within the week

absences.title: Absences
absences.intro: Mark when a care worker is not at work. The day plan then brings forward the visits whose worker is absent and does not offer that worker as a replacement. The reason is not asked here.
absences.no_workers: The organisation has no care worker yet (a person on some client's team).
absences.kind_hint: Planned is, for example, a holiday or training. The reason is not asked or stored.
absences.remove_confirm: Confirm: the absence was marked by mistake
absences.my_notice: An absence is marked for you today. Your visits today are in the coordinator's day plan.

obstacle.hint: You do not need to explain further. The coordinator sees the notice and your visits not yet done today.

kinds.LATE_30: I am about half an hour late
kinds.LATE_60: I am about an hour late

obstacle.sent_hint: The coordinator sees it in the day plan.
obstacle.handled_hint: The coordinator has looked at the notice.

week.title: Week plan
week.intro: Visits by worker and day, with absences. You can look about three months ahead. Press a day to open that day's plan; nothing is changed here.
week.heading: Week {week}: {from} to {to}
week.totals: Visits {visits}, planned time {amount}. Unassigned {unassigned}, worker absent {uncovered}.
week.empty: No visits are planned for this week.
week.legend: The number is the count of visits on that day. “absent” means an absence is marked for the worker; a number in that cell is the count of their uncovered visits. “open” are visits with no worker or whose worker is absent.

work_nature.title: Nature of the work
work_nature.none: No mark. Add one when the work here is heavy, so that the sharing of such visits between workers can be followed.
work_nature.kinds_label: What the work is like here
work_nature.kinds_hint: The mark describes the work, not the person. Choose all that apply.
work_nature.reason_hint: For example: lifting from bed to wheelchair without a hoist; stove heating and water from a well.
work_nature.heavy_visits: visits to clients marked as heavy work {count}
work_nature.worker_option: {name} (visits in 28 days: {count}; at clients marked as heavy work in total: {heavy})

precondition.title: Before the service starts
precondition.waiting: The service is waiting for a precondition: it does not start before this is met.
precondition.none: No preconditions. Add one when the service cannot start before something at home has been put right.
precondition.kind_label: What must be in order first
precondition.note_hint: For other, write what must be in order.
precondition.responsible_hint: By the home care guide the municipality arranges this. Write a name or a position.

keys.title: Keys
keys.none: The organisation holds no keys of this client. Add a key when the client hands one over.
keys.name: key no {tag}
keys.tag_hint: The tag carries only a number. The client's name or address is never written on a key: a lost key must not say whose door it opens.
keys.register_intro: All keys the organisation holds. Hand a key over or close it on the client's page.
keys.unreturned_title: Keys not returned (the service has ended)
keys.unreturned_empty: The organisation holds no keys of clients whose service has ended.

money.title: Client's money
money.intro: This is a record, not a payment: write down the cash the client gave you and what you did with it. Card details and PIN codes are never written here.
money.balance: You hold {amount} of this client's money.
money.balance_none: You hold none of this client's money.
money.note_hint: For spending, write what the money went on (for example shop or pharmacy).
money.holders_title: This client's money held by staff

supplies.title: Supplies
supplies.none: No supplies are followed. Switch on those whose running out would leave the client in trouble, for example firewood or drinking water.
supplies.note_label: Note (for example: enough for about three days)
supplies.responsible_hint: Write a name or a role: relative, care worker, municipality.

no_answer.title: If the door does not open
no_answer.none: No steps are agreed. Write down what you agreed with the client: what to do, and in which order, when the door does not open.
no_answer.steps_hint: Write in the client's own words and in the agreed order, up to {limit} steps. You can also write what is not to be done.
no_answer.emergency: If the person is in trouble or you fear the worst, call 112 and do what the emergency centre says.
no_answer.run_hint: Touch the steps you took. Each touch keeps the time; you do not have to write anything.
no_answer.recorded: The incident is recorded and the coordinator is notified.

review.keys_return: The organisation holds {count} of this client's keys: return them and mark them returned under keys.
review.money_return: Staff hold {amount} of this client's money: it has to be returned.
review.slots_end: The visit pattern still has {count} rows: end them, otherwise the visits continue when the client comes back to the service.
review.supplies_end: {count} supplies are followed: stop following them.
review.preconditions_open: {count} preconditions are open: mark them as no longer needed.
review.away_paused: Visits are paused. The visit pattern stays and the visits continue when you mark the client as on the service again.
review.away_keys: The organisation holds {count} of this client's keys. Agree who looks after the home (heating, pet, perishable food, post).

usual.title: Usual state
usual.none: The usual state has not been described yet. A description helps a covering worker notice when something is different.
usual.edit_hint: Write briefly how the client usually does. Write what can be seen, not a judgement. An area left empty is not shown.

examples.MOBILITY: For example: moves indoors with a rollator, does not use stairs alone
examples.EATING: For example: eats without help, drinks about a litre a day
examples.MOOD: For example: talkative, likes to speak about the grandchildren
examples.MEMORY: For example: knows the weekday, takes medicines without help
examples.SKIN_PAIN: For example: skin intact, knees ache in the morning
examples.HOME: For example: kitchen tidy, bed made

change.question: Was anything different from usual?
change.major: A big change: the coordinator has to know at once
change.yes_hint: Write below in one sentence what you saw. If the person needs help now, call 112 and the coordinator: this mark does not replace calling for help.
change.signals_hint: Care workers have noticed a change. Read their entries in the diary and mark what you did.

reasons.TWO_WORKERS: two care workers marked the same thing within two weeks
reasons.MAJOR: a care worker marked a big change

change.waiting_days: waiting for an answer for {days} days

crisis.title: Crisis readiness
crisis.none: Crisis readiness has not been assessed.
crisis.level_label: How much support is needed in a crisis

levels.DAILY: Needs a care worker's support every day
levels.WEEKLY: Needs support once or twice a week
levels.SELF: Manages alone for seven days with supplies

crisis.dependencies_hint: Mark what makes the situation worse quickly when it fails. May stay empty.

dependencies.ELECTRICITY: electricity (a device or an alarm button)

crisis.list_intro: Clients on the list: {count}. State on {date}. Download the list once a month and print it: in a crisis the application, the network or electricity may not work.
crisis.download_hint: The file opens in a spreadsheet. Keep the printout where it can be found without a computer.
crisis.group_time: Planned visit time a week in total {time}

referrals.title: Where to refer
referrals.none: There is no list yet. Put here the places a care worker can refer a person to when the question is not the care worker's job.
referrals.emergency: If the person is in danger, call 112.
referrals.edit_hint: Write the name of each place, the phone and when to turn to it. Check the numbers before saving: care workers have this list at hand on the phone. A row with an empty name is left out.

medication.pick: Choose what you did: reminding, seeing it taken and giving are different actions.
medication.missing: Choose at the medication activity what you did.
medication.open_count: The medication mark is missing on {count} visits. Ask the care worker.

workers.title: Workers
workers.intro: Each care worker's background check and trainings. Only the coordinator of the whole organisation sees this.
workers.empty: No care workers yet: a worker appears here once on a client's team.
workers.background_hint: Only the date of the check is recorded and, if you wish, when to check again. The result and its content are not written here.
workers.valid_label: Valid until or repeat by (if any)
